messages:
acme_csm: Hey team — ACME reports that after this morning's rollout their integration stopped receiving function calls from our API. They say model responses either omit the tool call entirely or the arguments are an empty object. Trace id they provided: trace-7f3b2a.

jenna_support: Thanks, can you paste an example of the request/response they sent? which model/variant and approx time?

acme_csm: Sure — customer was on hosted endpoint using `gptx-embed-001` variant (pinned). Timestamp ~2025-11-03T10:42:11Z. Their recorded response shows: 
```json
{
  "id": "resp_abc",
  "object": "response",
  "choices": [
    {
      "message": {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": null,
        "function_call": {
          "name": "create_invoice",
          "arguments": "{}"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
They say previously arguments would contain a JSON payload with line items.

jenna_support: OK that looks like args were stripped rather than a logic misfire. Any proxy or transform layers in front of the runtime?

leo_oncall: I noticed a config rollout earlier today to the request-transformer that normalizes empty strings and removes nulls. Deploy log: `deploy-bot: transform-service v2.14.0 -> active (1954321020)`. Could that have removed nested object fields?

mark_runtime: We intentionally added a sanitization step to remove extraneous empty fields from user metadata, but we scoped it to top-level keys. If the transformer has a bug that walks the whole JSON and removes empty objects, that could collapse `function_call.arguments` to `{}` or remove keys inside it.

acme_csm: Customer attached a repro curl they ran against our hosted API: 
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model":"gptx-embed-001",
    "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Create invoice for order 123","metadata":{"customer_id":"acme-79"}}],
    "functions":[{"name":"create_invoice","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array"}}}}]
  }'
```
Response showed a function_call with empty arguments.

leo_oncall: Can someone grep the transform-service change for a recursive prune? I can forward the customer's trace id to the infra logs: trace-7f3b2a.

infra-bot: Received trace lookup request for trace-7f3b2a. Found proxy hop: transform-service (10:42:09Z), runtime-gateway (10:42:10Z), runtime-node-12 (10:42:11Z). No 4xx from gateway.

mark_runtime: I pulled the runtime logs for that window — runtime received the request payload intact. The runtime emitted a model response with `function_call.arguments` populated (non-empty). The gateway's outgoing payload to the customer shows `arguments` replaced with `{}`. So the mutation happens after runtime, likely in transform-service/gateway.

jenna_support: Good detective work. So plan: 1) notify infra to rollback or hotfix transform rule, 2) gather a minimal repro we can run against prod to confirm, 3) offer customer a hotfix or rollback window.

leo_oncall: Quick repro I ran against the transform-service staging branch: POST body with nested `function_call.arguments` containing arrays/objects results in sanitizer converting arrays to `[]` and objects to `{}` when a new 'prune-empty' option is enabled. Repro steps in staging: 
```bash
# staging transform-service endpoint
curl -X POST https://staging-transform.redwood.internal/sanitize \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"function_call":{"name":"x","arguments":{"items":[{"sku":"A1","qty":1}]}}}'
# response: {"function_call":{"name":"x","arguments":{}}}
```
That matches customer behavior.

deploy-bot: deploy confirmed: transform-service config `prune-empty: true` enabled in prod at 1954321008 by mark_runtime (config change id cfg-7782).

mark_runtime: I pushed that config and assumed it was safe; I scoped it to user metadata but the sanitizer lib had a bug that walks the whole object. Rolling back now.

infra-bot: Rollback started for config cfg-7782. Expected completion ~10 minutes.

acme_csm: I told ACME we have a rollback in progress and will follow up once verified. They asked for a postmortem and timeline.

jenna_support: After rollback completes, can we run a regression test against ACME's example payload and confirm `function_call.arguments` is preserved? Also collect customer traces to validate messages delivered.

leo_oncall: I'll run automated check: run their curl against prod post-rollback and compare outgoing gateway body vs runtime emitted. I'll post diffs.

mark_runtime: Apologies for the regression — will add a unit test to prevent sanitizer from touching `function_call` or any key path matching `function_call.*`. Also will add an integration test that runs a few function-calling scenarios through the full stack.

acme_csm: Customer very happy we rolled back quickly. They asked when the fix will be permanent. I promised a short timeline and a follow-up PM.

jenna_support: Thanks everyone. Action items: mark_runtime = permanent fix + tests (ETA 48h), leo_oncall = verify prod repro + post rollback diffs (ETA 15m), infra = confirm rollback success and provide change log (ETA 10m), support = send customer interim update (I will).

leo_oncall: Verification complete: post-rollback the gateway outgoing body matches runtime and `function_call.arguments` preserved. trace-7f3b2a now shows full payload delivered to customer.

jenna_support: Closing loop with ACME and creating support ticket with root cause summary and timeline. We'll mark incident P2 and create a short postmortem once fix is merged. :thumbsup:

mark_runtime: Fix PR opened referencing cfg-7782 and test case (PR #4321). Will request expedited review.

acme_csm: Marking resolved on my side — customer confirmed their integration resumed normal behavior. Thanks team.
